title: Complexe de De Rham à puissance divisée [conférence de 1976 à l’IHÉS] : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting (continued from the previous page). A^\bullet_* is a bigraded object: for each n, A^\bullet_n is a cochain complex (think: polynomial or divided-power differential forms on the standard simplex Delta_n). It is simplicial in n, since a map Delta_m -> Delta_n induces restriction A_n -> A_m. M is a module. A Stokes-De Rham system is a family k_n : A^n_n -> M ('integration over Delta_n') satisfying the Stokes formula k_{n+1}(d omega) = sum_i (-1)^i k_n(partial_i omega). Such a system induces a map A^\bullet_* -> C^\bullet(Delta_*, M), sending omega to the cochain sigma |-> k_n(sigma^* omega). This realises Gamma(X, A) -> RGamma(X, M) for a simplicial set X.

The previous page imposes three hypotheses:
- a) A^i_n = 0 for i > n;
- b) H^n(A_n) = 0 for n >= 1;
- c) H^{n-1}(A_n) = 0 for n >= 2.

This page states the resulting classification and its consequences.

(1) The whole system (k_n) is determined by k_0 : A^0_0 = A_0 -> M. Proof by induction:
- By a) and b), A^n_n = Z^n_n = d A^{n-1}_n. So k_n(d eta) is forced to be sum (-1)^i k_{n-1}(partial_i eta).
- This is well defined if the right side vanishes on closed eta. For n >= 2, c) writes eta = d xi, and the double face sum cancels.
- For n = 1 the only obstruction is that k_0 must kill partial_1(Ker(A^0_1 -> A^1_1)). Here partial_1 is the boundary (difference of the two endpoint restrictions) of closed 0-forms on Delta_1.
- Hence k_0 extends iff k_0(partial_1 Ker d) = 0.

(2) There is therefore a 'universal Stokes-De Rham integration' with values in A_0 / partial_1(Ker d). The interesting case is partial_1(Ker d) = 0, where the universal target is A_0 itself. This holds under c'): closed 0-forms on Delta_1 are the constants pulled back via epsilon : Delta_1 -> Delta_0 (a degree-0 Poincare lemma, the n = 1 variant of c)). A marginal note gives the variant H^0(A_1) = epsilon^*(Z^0_0) for the general case, presumably without a).

(3) Consequently there is a homomorphism of (semi-)simplicial cochain complexes A^\bullet_* -> C^\bullet_{*M} extending k_0 (essentially the identity on A_0). It is unique by (1).

(4) It lands in normalized cochains C^{n!} (the intersection of kernels of degeneracies), because the value on a degenerate simplex factors through A^n_m = 0 for m < n. The next page checks this.

(5) The normalized n-cochains on Delta_m have basis the (n+1)-subsets of {0..m}. So C^{n!}_m is isomorphic to Lambda^{n+1}(free module on m+1 vertices) tensor M, i.e. Lambda^{*+1}Phi_* tensor M. Under this identification the coboundary is wedge with sum e_i.

Purpose: an axiomatic de Rham comparison theorem (integration map from a simplicial algebra of forms to cochains). It is to be applied on the next page to the divided-power polynomial de Rham complex of the simplex Gamma(T_0..T_m) tensor Lambda(dT) / (sum T_i - t)_pd over a pd-ring S, with t in the pd ideal, in order to get an integral/pd de Rham theorem.
errors: No substantive error. The induction (determination by k_0, obstruction only at n = 1) is correct under a), b), c).
Notation: partial_1 must be read as the alternating face sum (difference of endpoint restrictions), not a single face. Otherwise the obstruction is misstated.
The word 'unique' is struck or underlined ambiguously. Uniqueness does hold by the inductive argument.
'1/2 simpliciaux' is understated: defining the map on all simplices gives a fully simplicial map, which is in fact what step (4) uses.

ideas.what: Under acyclicity conditions a), b), c), a Stokes integration system k_n : A^n_n -> M is determined by k_0. The only obstruction is k_0 vanishing on the boundary of closed 0-forms on Delta_1.
ideas.modern_name: Axiomatic simplicial de Rham theorem / integration map from simplicial cdga of forms to cochains (acyclic-models type uniqueness)
ideas.usually_credited_to: H. Cartan, 'Théories cohomologiques' (1976); Sullivan (1977); Bousfield-Gugenheim (1976); Whitney for the classical case

ideas.what: Universal Stokes-De Rham integration with values in A_0 / partial_1(Ker d), which equals A_0 under a degree-0 Poincaré lemma c').
ideas.modern_name: Universal target of integration maps; degree-0 Poincaré lemma on Delta_1

ideas.what: The integration map lands in normalized cochains because A^n_m = 0 for m < n.
Identification of normalized cochains of Delta_m with Lambda^{n+1} of the free module on vertices (tensor M), with coboundary given by wedge with the sum of basis vectors.
ideas.modern_name: Exterior-algebra (Koszul-type) model of normalized cochains of the standard simplex; dual to Whitney elementary forms

missed.claim: Grothendieck sets up an axiomatic integration theorem (contemporaneous with Cartan's 'Théories cohomologiques') explicitly designed to apply to divided-power polynomial forms on simplices over a pd-ring. This is an integral/crystalline-flavoured PL de Rham theory. The later literature on integral simplicial pd-forms (e.g. Cenkl-Porter style work) does not cite or connect to this. The real novelty, the parametrised simplex sum T_i = t with t in the pd ideal, is on the next page, not this one.
missed.quote: le cas le plus intéressant est celui où ∂_1(Ker(A_1^0 → A_1^1)) = 0, donc où le dR universel est pour M = A_0
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Integral models of cochains via divided-power forms are of current interest (integral homotopy theory). This page only supplies the routine axiomatic framework.

deep.surprise_reason: Correct, but standard, axiomatic-de-Rham bookkeeping (uniqueness from k_0, normalization, exterior-algebra model of normalized cochains). Interesting mainly as context for the divided-power application on the next page.
transcription_corrections: Line 5: '(complexe [?] De Rham "universel"' should read '(Stokes-De Rham "universel"'.
'Λ^{*+1}Ω_{*h} ⊗_h M' is more likely 'Λ^{*+1}Φ_{*h} ⊗_h M' (consistent with Λ^{*+1}_S Φ_{*S} on the next page).
'il existe un [-unique-]': 'unique' is underlined, possibly struck; the status is ambiguous.
Marginal note: 'ou H^0(A_1^•) = ε^*(Z_0^0) dans le cas général' is plausible; the rest of the note is illegible.
